title: A Prayer When Betrayed
overview: A person hunted by enemies asks God for rescue, holds on to trust, and promises thanks as if the rescue has already come.

parts.label: A cry for rescue (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: The psalm's heading links it to the time people from the town of Ziph told King Saul where David was hiding (1 Samuel 23), so this is the prayer of someone betrayed close to home. Asking God to save "by your name" means appealing to who God is and his reputation for protecting people.

parts.label: Who the enemies are (v. 3)
parts.note: They are violent people out to kill him, who act as if God does not exist or will never hold them to account. Ancient copies differ between "strangers" and "arrogant" here, which is why translations read differently.

parts.label: Trust takes hold (v. 4)
parts.note: The mood shifts from pleading to confidence: God is the one who helps him and keeps him going. Older readings take one phrase to mean God stands among those who support him, or is the main one holding him up.

parts.label: Asking for justice (v. 5)
parts.note: He asks that the harm his enemies planned would come back on them, and that God would destroy them because God keeps his word. This is a frank prayer for his enemies' downfall, though he leaves the payback to God rather than taking it himself.

parts.label: Thanks promised (vv. 6-7)
parts.note: A freewill offering was a sacrifice no law required, given simply out of gratitude. He speaks of rescue as already done, which may be confidence ahead of time or a sign the psalm was finished after the danger passed; scholars are not sure which.

think: When people you trusted turn against you, what, if anything, helps you keep your footing?
